subject.title: [Feature]: Agent presentation tier: Control UI screen commands (splits/panels/sidebar) + agent terminal I/O

question: Should OpenClaw make agent-driven Control UI presentation a core capability now, and should agent terminal I/O be approved as part of the same roadmap or split behind a separate security design?
rationale: The UI command channel changes core gateway and Control UI product behavior, while terminal input creates a materially stronger execution and ownership boundary that cannot be selected safely from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Approve UI, split terminal
options.body: Proceed with capability-gated, reversible screen commands first and require a separate security-reviewed design issue for agent-owned terminal sessions.

options.title: Approve both phases
options.body: Sponsor both stacked phases with explicit protocol, approval, sandbox, PTY ownership, reconnect, and cleanup acceptance criteria before code review.

options.title: Keep operator-only
options.body: Retain the current operator-controlled UI and terminal model and close the capability roadmap as not planned.

recommendation.title: Approve UI, split terminal
recommendation.body: Proceed with capability-gated, reversible screen commands first and require a separate security-reviewed design issue for agent-owned terminal sessions.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature direction continues the agent-capabilities roadmap authored by the same person and carries the maintainer product signal.
